course_title: Seminar in the Art of the Ancient Americas, Africa, the African Diaspora, Islam and Asia: Material Devotions
subject: ARTHIST
course_description: Advanced seminar with emphasis on critical texts, methods, and techniques of art historical investigation. For art history majors; open to others with permission from the instructor.
course_notes: Materiality of Devotions, East & West This course brings together readings from both art history and religious studies, designed to provoke discussion about devotional practices in Asia and Europe. Our focus on material culture creates an opening for thinking about religions not as abstract beliefs but as bodily behaviors that are grounded in materials. The class is organized into themes that are relevant to both east and west, including the ways in which devotees physically represented their transcendent divinities, interacted with material remains of the divine, altered their own bodies to make connections with the sacred, conducted exalted rituals, and inscribed nature. A comparative approach has often been used in the study of religion. In applying it to art historical case studies, we seek to investigate humanity¿s shared devotional practices, while exploring the distinctive expression of each culture contextually. The sometimes strange and stimulating readings assembled will allow us to do just that. Art History major/minor: Division II or IV
